prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 36px · one-line width 36px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 78px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 56px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 60px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 67px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 619px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 629px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 628px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 629px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A weekly class timetable (grade י'2, semester א') read by day: a reader finds the day, then scans across the lesson block for time, subject, teacher and room, and finally reads the note that qualifies the lesson (homework, group split, room change, cancellation).","reading":"Right-to-left, top-to-bottom. The eye anchors on the merged day label, then runs leftwards through שעה → מקצוע → מורה → חדר, with הערות as an optional trailing annotation. Comparison is mostly vertical within a day (times march down in order) and across days for the same subject/teacher; the room number is the value a reader most often plucks out in isolation.","groups":["יום + שעה — the 'when' pair; the day cell is a merged anchor for 2–3 consecutive rows, so it frames the time column","מקצוע + מורה + חדר — the lesson identity triplet read as one sweep and the core of the scan","הערות — a separate annotation layer, not a peer of the triplet; it is prose, not a short field"],"keep_intact":["time ranges 08:15–09:00 etc. (78px unbreakable — must never break at the dash or wrap)","room values 204/112/305/210/118 and 'מעבדה 1'","teacher names (אבי שפירא, רונית לוי, מיכל אדרי)","subject names (מתמטיקה, תנ\"ך, היסטוריה)","day labels ראשון/שני/שלישי"],"may_wrap":["הערות — long free prose (up to 619px on one line); it may wrap to 2–4 lines and the merged day cell already gives those rows vertical room","header words שעה/מקצוע/מורה/חדר if needed, but only at word boundaries"],"note":"Only the widths are under control; total must stay ≤628px. Because the day column is row-merged, extra height from wrapped notes does not break the row-unit reading — but very long notes will visibly stretch the whole row."},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[57,99,77,81,88,226],"idea":"Spine at true minimums (each of יום/שעה/מקצוע/מורה/חדר gets exactly its one-line width) and every spare pixel to הערות, so notes read in 3 lines and the short fields never wrap — the most compact vertical table."},{"name":"B","widths":[60,110,80,85,93,200],"idea":"Give the scan-critical fields real slack — שעה gets 11px of breathing room so time ranges can never break at the dash, חדר and מורה get a few pixels — while הערות still takes roughly a third of the table."},{"name":"C","widths":[65,108,90,95,95,175],"idea":"Treat the lesson triplet מקצוע/מורה/חדר as three near-equal, calm columns and let הערות shrink to 175px (notes wrap to 3–4 lines); rows grow taller but the grid reads as an even rhythm rather than one dominant prose column."}]}
